headline: Researchers in New Zealand argue that most so-called Turing Tests ignore Alan Turing's own design, and that in a faithful version people spotted GPT-4-Turbo 97 percent of the time.
score_reason: Interesting study of how AI is judged, but small, tested one older model and comes from a university release.
importance_line: Readers who see headlines that AI has passed the Turing Test should note the result depends on test design, though the study tested only one older model with 37 people.
source: University of Canterbury, via Mirage News
summary: A University of Canterbury release, carried by Mirage News, says philosopher Diane Proudfoot, PhD student Sharon Temtsin and Professor Christoph Bartneck ran what they call the first experiment to follow Turing's open-ended, three-player imitation game, and 36 of 37 participants correctly picked out OpenAI's GPT-4-Turbo, taking 14 minutes on average. The authors argue no large language model has yet been shown to pass the original design, but stress that newer models may perform differently.
